title: BJP and Akali Dal set to revive Punjab alliance as Congress and SP near a UP seat deal
dek: Six years after the farm-law split, Amit Shah and Sukhbir Singh Badal called a joint press conference for Tuesday. In Uttar Pradesh, the opposition partners say their 2027 pact is days away.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The Bharatiya Janata Party and the Shiromani Akali Dal called a joint press conference at the BJP's headquarters in New Delhi for 1 pm on Tuesday, where they were expected to announce that they will fight the 2027 Punjab Assembly election together again, six years after the Akali Dal walked out of the National Democratic Alliance. Union Home Minister Amit Shah, BJP national president Nitin Nabin and Akali Dal president Sukhbir Singh Badal were to address it, according to reports. The announcement was timed for Guru Nanak Jayanti, the 557th Parkash Purab of the first Sikh Guru.

In Uttar Pradesh, which also votes in 2027, the Congress and the Samajwadi Party held their first formal round of seat-sharing talks in Delhi on Monday and said a deal was close. A second round was due on Tuesday.

## Punjab: an old alliance returns

The Akali Dal and the BJP were partners for 24 years until September 2020, when the Akali Dal quit the NDA over the three farm laws, which have since been repealed. Harsimrat Kaur Badal resigned from the Union cabinet at the time. Under their old arrangement the Akali Dal contested 94 of Punjab's 117 Assembly seats and the BJP 23, and in Lok Sabha elections the Akali Dal fought 10 seats and the BJP three.

Fighting separately in 2022, both were routed by the Aam Aadmi Party, which now governs the state: the BJP won two seats and the Akali Dal three. Some Punjab BJP leaders had earlier ruled out an alliance in public, according to reports.

Reports before Tuesday's press conference differed on the seat split. Some said the Akali Dal would remain the senior partner; others said the BJP wanted 40 to 55 seats, about twice its old share. Mr Shah said in Chandigarh on 1 November that the NDA would form Punjab's next government, according to reports. Asked about an alliance on 2 November, Mr Badal said: "You will come to know in a few days as to what will happen." He has said he is open to alliances with parties that accept his party's philosophy, except the Congress and AAP. Before the press conference, the Congress leader Sachin Pilot questioned whether the two parties had resolved the differences that split them in 2020 and called the move political opportunism, according to reports.

## Uttar Pradesh: 'things will be finalised tomorrow'

The Congress delegation, which included state president Aradhana Mishra 'Mona', the party's state in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam and MP Imran Masood, met the Samajwadi Party's Rajya Sabha MP Ram Gopal Yadav, state president Shyam Lal Pal and MPs Rajeev Rai and Iqra Hasan at the Delhi home of Congress MP Pramod Tiwari. Reports differ on how long the meeting lasted, from about 20 minutes to half an hour.

"We listened to each other's points of view. We will soon finalise this alliance," Mr Yadav said, adding that it would be done within two to three days. "Both parties are in agreement. They trust each other and will manage things jointly," Mr Gautam said. "Things will be finalised tomorrow," Ms Mishra said.

The Congress is seeking more than 100 of UP's 403 seats, and wants to contest at least one seat in every one of the state's 75 districts, according to reports citing party sources; one report put its opening demand at about 120 seats. The Samajwadi Party, the dominant partner, is inclined to offer far fewer, the reports said. The two parties fought the 2017 Assembly election together and the 2024 Lok Sabha election as part of the INDIA bloc, but contested the 2022 Assembly election separately.

## What happens next

The two states together send 93 members to the Lok Sabha. Details of the Punjab seat split were expected at Tuesday's press conference; in UP, the Congress and the SP said the allocation of constituencies would be taken up at Tuesday's second round. The Election Commission has not announced dates for either election.
